 In The Supreme Court Of India

(Arising out of SLP (C) 12223-12226 of 2022)
 UNION TERRITORY OF J K & ORS. 
 VERSUS  KHALID JEHANGIR BHAT & ORS. 
 O R D E R 1.
Leave granted.

2. We have heard Mr. Parth Awasthi, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellants and Mr.
Muzzaffar Khan, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the contesting respondents-original writ petitioners.

3. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order dated 28.10.2021 passed by the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh at Srinagar passed in Writ Petition Nos.
1993/2019, 1034/2020, 1410/2020 and 1070/2020, by which the Division Bench of the High Court has allowed the said Writ Petitions quashing and setting aside the notification issued under Section 4 of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, 1990 (for short the Act) and also the Award dated 20.02.2020,
the Union Territory of JK and others have preferred the present Appeals.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. From the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court, it appears that Writ Petition Nos. 1993/2019 & 1034/2020 were filed 16:52:06 IST Reason:
on behalf of the original writ petitioners challenging the notification issued under Section 4 of the Act as amended from time to time and Writ Petition Nos. 1410/2020 and 1070/2020 were filed challenging the Award dated 20.02.2020 declared under Section 11 of the Act.

sentences.text: By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court has set aside the notification issued under Section 4 mainly on the ground that there was no proper and valid publication of the notification as required under Section 4 of the Act inasmuch as the notification under Section 4 was not published in any newspaper of the regional language.
IA No. 23283/2023 has been filed on behalf of the appellants for placing on record additional documents.
It is the case on behalf of the appellants that,
as such
, the notification under Section 4 of the Act was, in fact, published in the newspaper of the regional language.

However, it is required to be noted that publication of Section 4 notification in the newspaper of regional language which is now sought to be produced on record was not placed before the High Court and, in fact, as observed by the High Court, the original record of the acquisition was also produced and the High Court perused the same and, as observed by the High Court, the record did not reveal or contain any newspaper of regional language in which the notification was published except the newspaper Aftab in Urdu language dated 19.05.2007 containing the notification dated 02.05.2017 issued under Section 4 of the Act, but the said notification was in English language.
Thus, the High Court opined that there was no publication of the notification in the regional language.

As the additional documents, which is now sought to be produced on record, was not even placed for consideration before the High Court and the same being disputed question of fact, we refuse to take on record the additional documents.

However, it will be open for the appellants to file a review petition before the High Court pointing out the additional documents, which are now sought to be produced as per IA No. 23283/2023 and as and when such review application is filed, the same be considered in accordance with law and on its own merits, subject to proving the same that the same was actually published, as sought to be contended now.

6. Now, so far as the findings recorded by the High Court that the Award dated 20.02.2020 was not published within the time is concerned, it is required to be noted that, while holding so, the High Court erroneously had considered the date of publication of Section 6 notification as 27.07.2017.
However, it appears that the declaration under Section 6 was published on 06.03.2018.
Under the circumstances, the Award passed on 20.02.2020 can be said to have been passed within the prescribed period.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the High Court that the Award dated 20.02.2020 was not within the time is hereby quashed and set aside.

7. Now, so far as the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court setting aside the Award dated 20.02.2020 on the ground that the same has been made under the repealed enactment and in clear violation of provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short the Act 2013) is concerned

[C.A.
Nos. 6778-6780 of 2022 decided on 12.10.2022], the Act 2013 shall not be applicable with respect to the acquisition under the Act.

8. In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court to the extent setting aside the Award dated 20.02.2020 on the ground that the same is in violation of the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of the Act 2013 is unsustainable and the same deserves to be quashed and set aside.

sentences.text: In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, the present appeals succeed in part in terms of the above.
The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court setting aside the Award dated 20.02.2020 is hereby quashed and set aside.

However, so far as the impugned judgment and order passing by the High Court quashing and setting aside the notification under Section 4 of the Act on the ground of non-compliance of the mandatory requirement under Section 4, namely, not publishing the notification under Section 4 in the newspaper in regional language is concerned, we reserve the liberty in favour of the appellants to file a review application, as observed herein above,
along with additional documents produced along with IA No. 23283/2023 and as and when such an application is filed, the same be considered in accordance with law and on its own merits, subject to proving the said additional documents and after giving an opportunity to the original writ petitioners.

However, at the same time, it is observed that in case the review application is dismissed in that case also, in light of the decision of this Court in the case of J&K Housing Board and Another vs. Kunwar Sanjay Krishan Kaul and Others (2011) 10 SCC 714, the proceedings will relate back to the stage of the objections under Section 5A of the Act and the acquisition proceedings be proceeded further from that stage.

necessary consequences shall follow.
The present appeals are partly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
No costs.
